guitar.evidence: Eric Johnson is renowned for his meticulously documented 1957/1962-style Fender Stratocaster tone (notably his guitar nicknamed 'Virginia') and has a Fender signature Stratocaster model.

tone.target: glassy EJ lead clean with slight compression, delay, and wah
tone.profile: glassy EJ lead clean with slight compression, delay, and wah
tone.summary: A pristine signal chain featuring compression and a gentle boost for articulation, followed by a bright, clean US Deluxe amp model paired with the US 2x12 cab. The tone is enhanced with a wah pedal and subtle delay to capture Eric Johnson's signature glassy lead sound.
corrections: Shift from jazz/blues clean to Eric Johnson lead clarity
Make wah part of the signature

rig.name: Eric Johnson - Desert Rose - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide smooth sustain and even out dynamics for lead articulation.
Incorporate the signature wah color and filter sweep.
Give the lead notes extra presence and clarity without adding grit.
blocks.gap: Using Boost for subtle lift, as a dedicated clean boost is not available.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the bright, clean Fender/Brilliant-style voicing required for EJ's tone.
Provide a bright and articulate cabinet voicing matching the clean US Deluxe amp.
Add subtle width and glassy movement without sounding overly wet.
blocks.gap: Chorus is optional, but adds a nice 'glassy' dimension often associated with this style.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle rhythmic echo and depth to the lead lines.
Provide minimal ambient space without creating a deep wash.
blocks.gap: Keeping reverb low is key to maintaining clarity and articulation.

improvements.summary: Enhance cabinet realism and articulation for glassy lead tones.

proposals.reason: Improve the natural, open sound of EJ's clean tone.
